records.label: Page-filling narrative scene
records.visual_function: Give one narrative image the spatial emphasis of a full page or dominant spread.
records.prompt: Expand the central narrative scene across the page, with one dominant visual event and supporting forms leading attention through the full image. Keep the essential action and setting readable at the larger scale, using the page edges as deliberate crop boundaries.
invariants: one scene or event carries the page-level emphasis
the large field has an intentional focal hierarchy
page edges support the selected crop
applicability: Chapter openings, major reveals, environmental scale, and expressive peaks.
Subject count, lettering, and rendering finish remain choices of the actual scene.
interactions: Supporting insets create a mixed layout when the narrative needs additional views.
Page-level prominence does not specify how long the depicted moment lasts.
A text-free solitary-character scene is one scoped variant.
misreadings_to_avoid: assuming a splash requires one character
assuming a splash forbids typography
stretching a minor beat without enough visual structure

misreading_policy.activation: use for review or a matching correction decision

records.label: Self-contained comic panel
records.visual_function: Make one framed moment communicate through staging, action, and optional lettering.
records.prompt: Compose one framed scene around a readable action or relationship. Give the important subjects and contacts clear silhouettes, and place any required speech, caption, or sound lettering in space that supports the scene's reading order.
invariants: one framed moment owns the composition
the central action or relationship is visible
lettering, when present, belongs to the same reading hierarchy
applicability: Single-panel comics, illustrated moments, and one panel within a larger sequence.
A silent panel is a scoped text-free variant.
interactions: The selected crop determines what can be shown directly.
A panel can contain several subjects without becoming several viewpoints.
A reaction and its hidden cause may need separate views instead of one overloaded panel.
misreadings_to_avoid: multiple incompatible camera views fused into one scene
assuming comic art requires speech balloons
assuming comic art excludes speech balloons

misreading_policy.activation: use for review or a matching correction decision

records.label: Vertical scroll reveal
records.visual_function: Control successive discoveries as the viewer moves down a continuous vertical sequence.
records.prompt: Stack the visual beats along a clear downward path, letting each scene occupy a distinct region. Use open intervals between major changes and place each reveal below the cue that prepares it. Repeat selected forms or background edges to carry continuity through the vertical space.
invariants: the sequence progresses downward
each reveal follows its preparing cue
spacing distinguishes related and separate beats
applicability: Scrolling comics, mobile illustrated stories, and vertical explanatory sequences.
The intended viewing window affects which beats are encountered together.
interactions: A tall single scene uses continuous spatial depth rather than sequential panels.
Long gutters change separation but do not specify exact reading time.
Lettering and image placement share the downward reading path.
misreadings_to_avoid: a reveal visible beside its setup when concealment matters
arbitrary blank space unrelated to the sequence
one tall panorama misread as several times or places

misreading_policy.activation: use for review or a matching correction decision

records.label: Different renderings in a shared scene
records.visual_function: Make differently rendered elements occupy the same depicted space while retaining their distinct visual treatments.
records.prompt: Give each selected element its own consistent rendering treatment, while their positions, relative scale, overlaps and contact points form one continuous scene. Carry the scene's light direction through the appropriate shading language of each element, with contact shadows and reflected color joining the visible surfaces where they meet.
invariants: each element retains its selected rendering treatment
perspective, scale and occlusion describe one shared space
contact and light response agree at the boundaries between treatments
applicability: A drawn subject inhabiting a photographic place, rendered objects within a painted setting, or another deliberate mixed treatment.
Use when interaction or contact between unlike renderings should feel spatially continuous.
interactions: A common light direction can be represented by different shading grammars.
Graphic overlays outside the depicted space keep their own flat relationships.
References contribute only their assigned content or rendering scope.
misreadings_to_avoid: all elements averaged into one unintended rendering style
contact or scale changing at the join between media
a flat explanatory mark treated as a physical object

misreading_policy.activation: use for review or a matching correction decision

records.label: Layered collage relationships
records.visual_function: Connect distinct image fragments through deliberate juxtaposition, overlap and visual hierarchy.
records.prompt: Arrange distinct image fragments around a clear focal cluster on a shared field. Keep their selected cut edges, crop boundaries and local textures visible. Use overlap, repeated shapes and directional alignment to connect related fragments, with open spacing that lets each important fragment remain recognizable.
invariants: fragment boundaries and layer order remain legible
juxtaposition expresses the selected relationships
each fragment retains its assigned content and treatment
applicability: Collage, photomontage, scrapbook, archival, music-cover and editorial constructions where association across fragments carries meaning.
Photographs, drawings, lettering and paper-like fields may contribute different roles.
interactions: Scale differences can be symbolic when the layout establishes separate fragment spaces.
A common palette or recurring edge treatment may unify unlike source materials.
Reading order and story chronology are selected independently from stacking order.
misreadings_to_avoid: incidental fragments obscuring the intended relationship
a montage treated as one continuous physical perspective
decorative source lettering replacing required wording

misreading_policy.activation: use for review or a matching correction decision

records.label: Image and information units
records.visual_function: Make related pictures, diagrams, symbols and facts readable as connected information units.
records.prompt: Group each picture or diagram with the wording and symbols that explain it. Give the leading unit greater visual weight, then align supporting units along shared edges with consistent internal spacing. Repeat the placement of equivalent labels and fields so their relationships remain clear across the composition.
invariants: each explanatory item has an identifiable subject or referent
equivalent information uses a consistent local hierarchy
visual importance follows the selected information priority
applicability: Editorial spreads, illustrated reports, exhibition panels, field guides, information cards, package faces and compact dashboards.
Use when several kinds of information need a shared reading structure; the artifact determines its units and density.
interactions: A continuous image may cross unit boundaries while labels retain clear associations.
Photographic evidence, drawn explanation and text can use different local treatments.
An actual card face, a page design and a photograph of either have different framing requirements.
Facts, quantities and exact wording retain their source meaning; visual grouping supplies no new data.
misreadings_to_avoid: decoration or invented data filling every available field
labels detached from the picture or diagram they explain
equal visual emphasis hiding the main information

misreading_policy.activation: use for review or a matching correction decision

records.label: Interface and illustration relationships
records.visual_function: Explain a selected screen state or concept through the relationship between interface regions and visual content.
records.prompt: Organize the principal visual content and selected interface regions on a shared alignment system. Keep related labels, controls and status marks grouped, with clear scale and active-state contrast. Connect explanatory symbols or diagrams to their corresponding screen content, and preserve essential words and depicted features through the chosen overlaps.
invariants: each interface region has a selected informational role
labels and controls remain associated with their visible referents
interface geometry and depicted scene geometry keep their declared relationship
applicability: Static application or game screens, visual-novel compositions, illustrated interfaces, and conceptual explanations built from interface fragments.
Choose the fidelity of the interface from the information the artifact must communicate.
interactions: A visual-novel scene can share the field with dialogue or choices when those elements belong to the intended moment.
A HUD can remain flat over a spatial scene; a physical display belongs to the scene perspective.
Conceptual simplification and exact screen reproduction need different text and detail choices.
The depicted state does not establish functioning controls or an implemented application.
misreadings_to_avoid: interface decoration substituted for meaningful state or information
unrequested browser or device furniture changing the intended screen format
necessary wording reduced to illegible placeholder marks

misreading_policy.activation: use for review or a matching correction decision
